items.followUp: Write the subshell electronic configurations of oxygen and magnesium.

rubric.why: Checks the complete subshell configuration of sodium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹, including all subshells in the correct order and with correct electron counts.

rubric.why: Checks the complete subshell configuration of carbon.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 1s² 2s² 2p², including all subshells in the correct order and with correct electron counts.

items.followUp: Write any two features of the long form of the periodic table.

rubric.why: A key feature is the basis on which elements are arranged.
rubric.description: Elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that elements are arranged by increasing atomic number.

rubric.why: The table's periods, groups, and their relationships are defining features.
rubric.description: Any one other correct feature of the long form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct feature, such as 7 periods and 18 groups, similar properties within a group, or the same number of electron shells for elements in a period.

modelAnswer: Elements in the long form of the periodic table are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
The table has 7 periods and 18 groups; elements in the same group have similar chemical properties.

items.followUp: Define ionization energy and state why it generally decreases down a group.

rubric.why: The definition identifies the attraction for bonding electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electronegativity is an atom's tendency to attract the shared pair of electrons in a covalent bond.

rubric.why: The reason for the trend is the weaker attraction for bonding electrons farther from the nucleus.
rubric.description: Correct reason for the decrease down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that increasing atomic size and/or shielding reduces the nucleus's attraction for the shared electrons.

modelAnswer: Electronegativity is the ability of an atom to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself in a covalent bond.
Down a group, atomic size and shielding increase, so the nucleus attracts the shared electrons less strongly; therefore, electronegativity generally decreases.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding requires hydrogen to be bonded to a strongly electronegative atom.
rubric.description: Identifies the hydrogen atom involved in hydrogen bonding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that hydrogen is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom, usually F, O, or N.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding is an intermolecular attraction involving another electronegative atom.
rubric.description: Identifies the intermolecular attraction that forms the hydrogen bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the attraction between that hydrogen and a lone pair on a highly electronegative atom in the same or another molecule.

modelAnswer: A hydrogen bond is an intermolecular attraction involving a hydrogen atom covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom, usually F, O, or N.
The hydrogen is attracted to a lone pair on a highly electronegative atom of the same or a neighbouring molecule.

rubric.why: Evaporation takes place as energetic molecules leave the liquid surface.
rubric.description: Identifies surface molecules with sufficient kinetic energy as those that escape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that surface molecules with sufficient kinetic energy escape from the liquid.

rubric.why: The continuing escape of molecules explains why evaporation is continuous.
rubric.description: Explains that evaporation continues as molecules keep escaping.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that molecules continuously escape from the surface (or that evaporation can occur at all temperatures).

modelAnswer: Molecules in a liquid are in continuous motion, and some surface molecules always have enough kinetic energy to escape into the air.
As these molecules keep escaping from the surface, evaporation is a continuous process.

items.followUp: Define a solute and a solvent. What is a dilute solution?

rubric.why: A solution consists of a solute and a solvent uniformly mixed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a solution as a homogeneous mixture of a solute and a solvent.

rubric.why: An aqueous solution is specifically a solution whose solvent is water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an aqueous solution is a solution in which water is the solvent.

modelAnswer: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of a solute and a solvent.
An aqueous solution is a solution in which water is the solvent.

items.followUp: What is meant by a saturated solution?

rubric.why: An unsaturated solution has not yet reached its solute limit at the stated temperature.
rubric.description: States that the solution can dissolve more solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an unsaturated solution contains less than the maximum amount of solute it can dissolve at that temperature.

rubric.why: The amount of solute a solution can hold depends on temperature.
rubric.description: Relates the definition to a particular temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying that the solution can still dissolve more solute at the given temperature.

modelAnswer: An unsaturated solution contains less solute than the maximum amount that can dissolve in the solvent at a given temperature.
Therefore, more solute can still dissolve in it at that temperature.

items.followUp: Write the names of any four highly reactive metals.

rubric.why: Credit is given for correctly naming metals from the moderately reactive group.
rubric.description: Names any two moderately reactive metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two of zinc, iron, tin, and lead.

rubric.why: The question asks for four metals, so the full set of four names earns the remaining mark.
rubric.description: Names the remaining two metals to give four correct names.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the answer names all four: zinc, iron, tin, and lead.

modelAnswer: Four moderately reactive metals are zinc, iron, tin, and lead.
